title: Bechet's influence on New Orleans jazz in France
summary: She says Bechet's arrival and settling in France sparked young orchestras, that his commercial records drew young listeners, and that his and Reveliotti's deaths ended a form of jazz in France. She notes his repertoire was more modern than Merlin and Atlan's.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom

blocks.x: Also, you told me about the effect of Bechet on New Orleans jazz in France. How he changed.

Well, in fact, the influence of Bechet was really preponderant, because before him, of course, there was the Claude Luther's orchestra. There were some concerts with Louis Armstrong, who came to France, and who had a crazy success. But it was the arrival of Bechet in France, and the fact that he was fixed, that everything decided, that really created a terrible jazz jazz in New Orleans. At this moment, there were a lot of young orchestras who were created, who played, of course, with Bechet, and especially André Reveliotti. And Bechet, at the beginning, he did a little commercial music, I think, with the recordings like The Oignons, The Rue d'Antibes, and all that. And then, it had a good side, but it had a good side, because these recordings were commercial which allowed some young people to get interested in this music. And then, after, he played things less commercial, and the people liked it. The work was finally done, at the moment.
Did you... I don't understand French, Edwin. Do you have many old Bechet records? Have you heard many of his old records?
Is that what you were saying?
No. It was more commercial in France.
Go ahead with what you were saying. I interrupted you there. Well, I think it was a symbol of Bechet. Because he had a lot of importance. It was a symbol of Bechet.
Because he had a lot of importance. After his death, it was almost done. It was a symbol of Bechet. And then, after what you were saying, I interrupted you there.

Well, I think it was a symbol of Bechet. I said that it was actually allowed many young French people to be interested in the Jazz Nouvelle Orléans. And, unfortunately, when he died... In fact, it was a symbol of Bechet. Because he had a lot of importance. After his death, it was almost done. It was almost done. There were still some orchestras who played, some young people who interested, but many less. And I think that the death of Bechet and the death of Reveliotti, a little after him. Reveliotti, they played very long with Bechet, three years, I think. After that Bechet had ceased to play with Luther, he played with Reveliotti, always. And the death of Bechet and Reveliotti were the end of a certain form of jazz in France. In fact, Bechet, when he was in France, he didn't really play the old style Nouvelle Orléans as you can listen to here or like Jospin, Merlin and Atlan. It was already more modern. It was already the same theme. It was more modern in the style and in the choice of the theme, I think. It wasn't the orchestras, the parade, the things of that genre. With the blues, obviously, it was always the blues. But all the themes that I heard, recorded by Bechet, during the time he played in France, were more recent themes. And often the compositions that he had made just before his death, or when he was in France. And he played, finally, pretty few themes. Except, obviously, Scratch Trumble or White Society, when people asked him, because people knew his airs, so they asked him. But, otherwise, he didn't play the same airs, even when I heard him record in the 1930s or before, 1925, when he played with... What do they call him? When he recorded with Armstrong, Charles Williams, all that.
